FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft 
finalized by the Ready-to-Eat Foods and Specialized Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Food and Agriculture Division Council. 


Chewing gum was originally made of the prime raw material called ‘chicle gum’ which was imported; sugar and 
flavourings agents were added to make the chew more palatable. With the increase in demand for these 
products, and the short supply of chicle gum, considerable research was undertaken and several substitutes 
of natural and synthetic gums were developed in the country. This standard incorporates the list of indigenous 
gums and other recommended ingredients for gum base and prescribes other essential requirements of chewing 
gums. Chewing gum is offered to consumers in several forms. Candy coated gum in rectangular pillow or ball 
shape, stick or slab gum, double gum in toffee shape are some of the varieties common in the Indian market. 


This standard was first published in 1972 and revised in 1981. In the first revision the lists of recommended 
ingredients and sources for gum base and optional ingredients for chewing gum were made more extensive. 
The method for determination of gum base content was also modified. 


In this second revision, the following modifications have been carried out: 
a) The title and scope has been modified to specify requirements for chewing gum only as bubble gum 
is a subset of chewing gum; 
b) The list of permitted sweeteners and optional ingredients has been expanded; 
c) New types of chewing gums have been added in the standard; 
d) The requirements for gum base and acid insoluble ash have been modified; and 


e) The requirements for moisture, sulphated ash, reducing sugar and sucrose have been deleted as 
they no longer seem relevant. 


In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Food Safety 
and Standards Act, 2006 and the Rules framed thereunder and the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) 
Rules, 2011. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in 
the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 6747 : 2018 


Indian Standard 
CHEWING GUM — SPECIFICATION 


(Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and 
methods of sampling and test for chewing gum.

3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definition shall apply. 


3.1 Chewing Gum 


Chewing gum is generally a food which is made from 
a natural or synthetic gum base containing 
flavourings and flavouring compounds, sweeteners 
(nutritive or non-nutritive) and other additives. It 
includes bubble gum and breath-freshener gum 
products. Bubble gum is a chewing gum, the gum 
base of which is strong and elastic enough to stretch 
and form a bubble when filled with air insufflated 
through the mouth by chewing gum consumer. 


4 ESSENTIAL INGREDIENTS 


4.1 Gum Base — Natural or synthetic, non-toxic 
gum base shall be used. List of recommended 
ingredients or sources thereof are given in Annex A. 


4.2 Sweeteners — It may contain one or more 
sweeteners such as: 


a) Nutritive Sweeteners — Cane jaggery 
(see IS 12923); Palm jaggery (see IS 13952); 
Palm sugar (see IS 14400); Raw sugar 
(see IS 5975); Khandsari (see IS 13953); 
Invert sugar, Honey (see IS 4941); Sorbitol 
(see IS 4750); Liquid glucose (see IS 873); 
Lactose, Dextrins, Dextrose (see IS 874); 
Dextrose monohydrate, Maltose and Icing 
sugar (see IS 1152); Sugar (see IS 1151 or 
IS 5982); Bura sugar (see IS 12924) 


b) Non-Nutritive Sweeteners — Artificial 
Sweeteners and/or Polyols. 


4.3 Flavour and Flavouring Compounds — The 
product(s) shall contain flavour and flavouring 
compounds as permitted under the Food Safety and 
Standards (Food Products Standards and Food 
Additives) Regulations, 2011. 


IS 6747 : 2018 


5 OPTIONAL INGREDIENTS 


5.1 In addition to the essential ingredients specified 
under 4, the following additional ingredients may also 
be used: 
a) Malt; 
b) Dairy and dairy analogues such as milk, milk 
products, whey, casein etc; 


c) Chocolate, chocolate derived products (for 
example cocoa powder (defatted or not), 
cocoa mass, etc) or any extract thereof; 


d) Coffee, chicoree, tea or any extract thereof; 
e) Gelatin; Food grade; 

f) Edible starches; 

g) Edible oil seed flour; 


h) Spices and condiments and their extract 
thereof; 


j) Baking powder; 
k) Edible vegetable fats and oils; 
m) Protein isolates; 


n) Fruits, vegetables and their products; in any 
form suitable to product; 


p) Nuts and nut products; 

q) Water, potable (it is drinking water); 

r) Nutrients such as vitamins, minerals etc; 

s) Edible gums; 

t) Salt (in any form such as common salt, 
iodized salt, rock salt, black salt etc); 


u) Other edible fillings or ingredients; 


v) Any other ingredient appropriate to the 
product; and 


w) Proprietary product 
6 TYPES 


For the purpose of this standard, there are following 
types of chewing gum products: 


6.1 Stick/ Tab/ Slab/ Chunk 


Chewing gums in various shapes and sizes like stick/ 
tab/slab/chunk. Sticks are usually flat. Tab/slab are 
thicker than sticks. Chunks are thicker than tab/slab. 


6.2 Pellet 


Pellet chewing gum, also called ‘pellet gum’ or simply 
‘pellet’, is a chewing gum with a heart of gum base 
surrounded with a coating. 


6.3 In roller 


Chewing gum-in-roller is sold in a distributing device 


named chewing gum roller. Chewing gum in the roller 
is in fact a long slab enrolled around a single axe. 


6.4 Powdered/Granulated 


Powdered chewing gum is a type of granulated 
chewing gum generally sold in a small size bag or 
pack, forming one serving per bag or pack. The 
powdered particles of chewing gum will reconstitute 
a piece of chewing gum after a few moment of 
mastication of the powdered chewing gum under the 
effect of the moisture present in the saliva of the 
consumer. 


6.5 Compressed 


Compressed chewing gum is a chewing gum product 
which is formed by one or more layers of chewing 
gum and eventually other confectionery part. 
Compressed chewing gum products can have infinity 
of different shapes from a pastille -like shape to any 
figurine-like shape. 


6.6 Center-filled/ Filled Gums/ Gums with Toppings 
Chewing gum prepared with filling or topping or 


layering, having the combination of ingredients as 
permitted in 4 and 5. 


6.7 Liquid Gum 


The gums made with ingredients as permitted 
under 4 and 5, having liquid or semi-solid 
consistency. 


6.8 Other Types 


Chewing gum can take a lot of different shapes than 
those described in 6 and be also a part of other 
confectionery products (for example a centered part 
of a sugar coated lollipop). 


7 REQUIREMENTS 
7.1 General 


Chewing gum product shall meet following general 
requirements: 
a) Besafe and suitable for human consumption. 


b) Bein any desired shape, size or colour with 
pleasant taste and flavour. 


c) Be free from dirt and other harmful or 
injurious foreign matter. 


d) Not be brittle or gritty but smooth and with 
characteristic chewability. 


7.2 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1 and Table 2.

8 PACKING AND MARKING 
8.1 Packing 


The material, if wrapped, shall be in plain or printed 
cellulose film, waxed paper, aluminium foil, 
polyethylene or other flexible packaging materials. 
In the case of printed packaging material, the printing 
ink shall not come into direct contact with the gum. 
If the printing ink comes into direct contact it shall 
be non-toxic. The wrapped or unwrapped material 
shall be bulk packed or further packed in clean, 
reasonably airtight and sound containers. Such 
containers shall be made of tinplate, glass, plastics, 
thermoplastic material, moisture-proof paper, 
cellulose film or any other suitable packaging material 
including flexible material. 


IS 6747 : 2018 


8.2 Marking 


Each package shall be marked or labelled with the 
following particulars: 


a) Name and type of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Net mass of the contents in grams; 

d) Date of manufacture or code number 
indicating the date of manufacture; 

e) List of additives, if used; 

f) Manufacturer’s licence number; 

g) The words ‘Best before ........ (Month and 
year to be indicated); and 


h) Any other requirement as stipulated under 
Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and 
regulations framed thereunder and Legal 
Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 
2011. 


8.3 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


8.3.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
2016 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 
The details of conditions under which the licence 
for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards 


9 SAMPLING METHODS 


9.1 Representative samples of chewing gum 
products shall be drawn as prescribed in 3 of IS 6287. 


10 METHODS OF TESTS 


10.1 Methods of analysis shall be as prescribed in 
the appropriate clauses. 


10.2 Quality of Reagents 


10.2.1 Unless otherwise specified, laboratory grade 
chemicals and distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be 
employed in the tests.

A-5 ANTIOXIDANTS 


A-5.1 All antioxidants permitted in chewing gum (see 
Horizontal Standard on the Use of Food Additives in 
Chewing gum and generally in food at GMP level) 
can be used in gum base provided that the 
concomitant addition of such antioxidants in gum 
base part and in the chewing gum part does not lead 
to exceed the maximum permitted use level in final 
chewing gum, in accordance with the principles set 
out in section 4.2 of the Preamble of the Codex 
alimentarius General Standard on Food Additives 
(CODEX STAN 192-1995, latest version). 


ANNEX B 
(Clauses 7.2) 


DETERMINATION OF GUM BASE CONTENT 


B-1 PREPARATION OF THE SAMPLE 


B-1.1 Take four tablets of chewing gum or bubble 
gum and clean with a fine hair brush to remove talc 
and sugar dust. Cut the sample into small pieces. 


B-2 METHOD 


B-2.1 Weigh accurately the entire sample and 
quantitatively transfer the sample into an extraction 
catridge. Take 200 ml of chloroform in a tared 250 ml 
capacity round-bottom flask. Extract the sample for 
eight hours in a soxhlet extraction assembly. 
Subsequently distil off the chloroform in a drying 
chamber at 105°C + 1°C. Weigh the flask. Continue 
the process till a constant mass is obtained. 


B-3 CALCULATION 


B-3.1 Gum base content, percent 


M,-M,x100 
by mass = M 
where 
M, = mass in g of the flask with extracted gum 
sample, 
M, = mass in g of the empty flask, and 
M = mass in g of the sample taken for test

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed

needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of
